questions.prompt: What makes the Intuit chapter a connection company case?
choices: It shows connection as a company story about linked execution across adjacent work
It proves every team should merge into one stream
It replaces coordination with more meetings

explanation.gentle: The chapter takes connection out of theory and into a company case.
explanation.direct: Its main job is to show how linked execution keeps adjacent work from splitting apart.
explanation.competitive: This case is about real linkage, not louder collaboration.

questions.prompt: How does the chapter distinguish connection from parallel streams?
choices: Connection begins when dependency handoffs and linked priorities become visible
Connection means each team protects its own flow without adjustment
Connection requires one centralized stream for all work

explanation.gentle: The company becomes more connected when teams can see how work passes between them.
explanation.direct: The chapter says visible handoffs are the difference, not just adjacent effort.
explanation.competitive: Hidden breaks mean separate streams, not connection.

questions.prompt: Why is communication volume a weak substitute for connection in this chapter?
choices: Because more talk can still leave operational linkage weak
Because the chapter rejects all discussion
Because connection means no handoffs are needed

explanation.gentle: The chapter separates talking more from linking work better.
explanation.direct: Discussion is weaker than visible handoffs and linked priorities.
explanation.competitive: Chatter is not a stream map.

questions.prompt: Avery sees adjacent teams with strong local plans but unclear handoffs. What best fits the chapter?
choices: The company is connected because both teams are serious
The company needs visible handoffs and linked priorities before calling the work connected
The company should hide the handoff issues until later

explanation.gentle: Serious local plans are weaker than visible linkage between adjacent work.
explanation.direct: The missing piece is operational connection, not more parallel effort.
explanation.competitive: Parallel streams are not linked execution.

questions.prompt: A theater production board worked hard but kept discovering breaks between subgroups late. What chapter failure does this show?
choices: Healthy specialization with no downside
Fragmented streams caused by weak visible handoffs
Too much visible linkage

explanation.gentle: The problem is weak linkage, not weak effort.
explanation.direct: The board let adjacent streams stay poorly connected.
explanation.competitive: They had one production and several private flow lines.

questions.prompt: Which misreading does the chapter reject?
choices: Connection means more communication alone
Connection depends on visible handoffs
Connection links adjacent work across dependencies

explanation.gentle: The chapter says more discussion is weaker than operational linkage.
explanation.direct: Communication volume is a substitute, not the mechanism.
explanation.competitive: If more chatter is your answer, you missed the company lesson.

questions.prompt: What is happening when teams work hard but the streams between them remain weakly linked?
choices: Real connection is already complete
Fragmented flow is weakening the whole effort
The chapter says handoffs no longer matter

explanation.gentle: Weak handoffs let execution split even when teams mean well.
explanation.direct: The chapter treats fragmented streams as the key company failure pattern.
explanation.competitive: Broken flow still wins under coordination language.

questions.prompt: A mentoring network wants stronger connection without forcing one centralized stream. Which judgment best fits the chapter?
choices: The network should reject visible handoffs
The network should keep distinct work but make the handoffs visibly concrete
The network should flatten every group into one flow

explanation.gentle: Connection can link distinct work without erasing it.
explanation.direct: The chapter favors visible handoffs over centralization theater.
explanation.competitive: The map matters more than one giant pipe.

questions.prompt: What deeper point does the chapter make about visible handoffs in a company?
choices: They matter only after work has already broken
They turn coordination into something operational before fragmented flow becomes costly
They belong only to communication style and not to execution

explanation.gentle: Visible handoffs help teams repair breaks before the cost rises.
explanation.direct: The chapter makes linkage part of execution rather than just of tone.
explanation.competitive: See the break early or pay for it later.

questions.prompt: Why does Chapter 9 naturally lead into tracking and accountability next?
choices: Because once work is linked, the next issue is whether the connected movement is visible and owned
Because connection removes the need for measurement
Because company stories end after connection

explanation.gentle: The bridge asks how teams track the movement of connected work.
explanation.direct: After linkage comes the question of owned visible progress.
explanation.competitive: Once the streams connect, the next fight is proof of motion.
